subject: CHECKING VERBOSE: MODEL WITH TWO INDEPENDENT RANDOM EFFECTS

messages.author: bb723ef8c9a6e579
messages.subject: CHECKING VERBOSE: MODEL WITH TWO INDEPENDENT RANDOM EFFECTS
parts:
Dear INLA users,

I am trying to fit a Poisson model with three covariates and two random effects. I have selected default prior distributions for precisions of this effects. After to fit the model I check the verbose, and It displays the message: "Mode not sufficient accurate; switch to a stupid local search strategy."

In addition, I check the eigenvalues of the hessian and one of them seems to be a large value:

"610" "  1088.329116    -2.566999"
"611" "    -2.566999    17.623737"
"612" "Eigenvectors of the Hessian"
"613" "        0.999997        0.002397"
"614" "        -0.002397        0.999997"
"615" "Eigenvalues of the Hessian"
"616" "        1088.335270"
"617" "        17.617582"
"618" "StDev/Correlation matrix (scaled inverse Hessian)"
"619" "     0.030318     0.018535"
"620" "                  0.238246"


Moreover, I also look the compute corrected stdev for thetas, and the positive value of the first hyperparameter seems to be far from 1.

"622" "Compute corrected stdev for theta[0]: negative 1.000000  positive 0.458808"
"623" "Compute corrected stdev for theta[1]: negative 1.117176  positive 0.896709"

 I have tried modifying the priors, and the results are always the same and the message appears again. How can I solve that?, Can I trust in this result? I enclose the verbose.

Thanks for everything!!! :)

Best regards,

Joaquín.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] CHECKING VERBOSE: MODEL WITH TWO INDEPENDENT RANDOM EFFECTS
parts:
Hi

In such cases I usually add

r = inla(....)
r = inla.rerun(r)

and then its usually solves itself. the problem is that the model is
only weakly identifiable, so more informative priors will also help (or
more informative data, which is usually not possible).

Best
H
